description:
Pass 1 expanded ALLOWED_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS to include NameConstraints, CertificatePolicies, PolicyMappings, PolicyConstraints, InhibitAnyPolicy, EKU, SAN, and IssuerAltName. However, CRITICAL_OK_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS still only contains BasicConstraints and KeyUsage.

In check_extensions, any extension OID that is in ALLOWED_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS but NOT in CRITICAL_OK_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS will cause UnhandledCriticalExtension when marked critical (line 523). For several of the newly-added OIDs this is always the case in practice:

- NameConstraints: RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 says it MUST be critical.
- InhibitAnyPolicy: RFC 5280 §4.2.1.14 says it MUST be critical.
- PolicyConstraints: RFC 5280 §4.2.1.11 SHOULD be critical.

So adding NameConstraints (and the others) to ALLOWED_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS while not adding them to CRITICAL_OK_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS means verify_simple will always reject real-world intermediates carrying these extensions. pkix-path handles all these OIDs as critical (HANDLED_CRITICAL_OIDS), so CRITICAL_OK_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS should be expanded to match.

Fix: Add OID_EXT_NAME_CONSTRAINTS, OID_EXT_CERTIFICATE_POLICIES, OID_EXT_POLICY_MAPPINGS, OID_EXT_POLICY_CONSTRAINTS, OID_EXT_INHIBIT_ANY_POLICY, OID_EXT_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE, OID_EXT_SUBJECT_ALT_NAME to CRITICAL_OK_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS (matching the set that pkix-path already handles in HANDLED_CRITICAL_OIDS).
title: pkix-chain-simple: CRITICAL_OK_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS too narrow after ALLOWED_INTERMEDIATE_EXTENSIONS expansion
